records.text: Victor Marx called FoldAR the best available product for engaging a hostile threat in a school.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: Well, I'll tell you, everyone knows that time in a critical life and death situation makes the biggest difference. ... And this weapon platform, not only being an outstanding high end platform to shoot, it is absolutely the best product in order to engage a hostile threat in a school, bar none.

records.text: Victor Marx said he wanted every school resource officer in Texas, and eventually throughout the United States, to receive a FoldAR.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: And again, with it being carried in a backpack. It keeps the level of anxiety down for students to watch. So we know this is a lifesaver and what we want to do is to be able to see every resource officer first starting the state of Texas have one of these and then it's spreading throughout the United States so that our children will be made safe.

verification.notes: The episode plays a recording of Marx stating that he wanted every resource officer in Texas to have the FoldAR and then wanted the effort to spread throughout the United States. The statement accurately represents his publicly recorded promise.

sources.title: Candace Episode 329 transcript with Victor Marx clip
sources.relevance: Transcribes Marx directly stating the Texas-first and nationwide school-resource-officer goal.

records.text: Candace Owens said Evergreen High School's full-time resource officer was on medical leave and a deputy primarily assigned to Conifer High School was covering both schools part-time on the shooting date.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Well, Evergreen High School did have a full-time school resource officer position, but the deputy that was assigned to that role happened to be on medical leave at the time of the shooting. ... So a different deputy whose primary assignment was actually another high school that was nine miles away, Conifer High School, was filling in part-time. ... So he was working as the school officer for both Conifer High School and Evergreen. Evergreen. He was the only one that was on duty the day of the shooting.

verification.notes: JCSO and contemporaneous reporting confirm that the regular Evergreen school resource officer was on extended medical leave. A substitute assigned across Evergreen and Conifer was at Evergreen that morning, returned to Conifer, and was sent toward a nearby crash before the shooting call redirected the deputy.

sources.title: JCSO Evergreen High School Shooting Investigation Update
sources.relevance: Official release confirms the shared Evergreen-Conifer assignment and deputy movements.

sources.title: Evergreen High School resource officer left just before shooting
sources.relevance: Independent reporting confirms the regular officer was on medical leave and a substitute was covering.
